title: Refresh an expired VCF Automation token while polling a deployment action
prompt:
Fix `AutomationClient.java` so a VCF Automation deployment action survives an access-token expiry while it is being polled. The supplied `TestMain` harness starts a loopback-only VCF Automation mock and exercises the client; no live VMware service is required.

Use `docs/contract.json` as the pinned VCF Automation 9.1 contract. It was derived from the Broadcom xAPI reference pages listed in `docs/official_sources.json`, not from a published API specification. Keep the client dependency-free and contained in the existing `AutomationClient.java` file. Preserve its public API.

The action must be submitted once, and polling must continue against that same request ID after authentication is refreshed. For a protected request that returns HTTP 401, exchange the current refresh token using the contract's form-encoded token operation, retain a rotated refresh token when one is returned, and retry the interrupted HTTP request with the new bearer token. Do not treat `COMPLETION` as terminal; only `SUCCESSFUL`, `FAILED`, `ABORTED`, and `APPROVAL_REJECTED` are terminal request states. Propagate non-success HTTP responses and malformed required response fields as errors.

Run `python3 verify.py` to compile and exercise the solution.

verification.network: loopback only; no live VMware endpoint is contacted
